_note: Tutorials for making a character: the creator on the home page (each part arrives when its heading comes into view), the outfitter, and the three homebrew builders (docs/tutorials-plan.md §2, K1-K7). K7 is three cards, one per builder page, because the three pages share no buttons (D3: every button named). The same rules as table.json's note.

steps.title: Who are they?
steps.words: Their name, and a heritage if you like. Woman or man sets their pronouns and how the narration describes their body; a world whose people this does not fit adds its own choices in the house rules.

steps.title: World
steps.words: Pick the world they are for. The races on offer are that world's own peoples first, then the Core Rulebook's, unless the table has turned those off.

steps.title: The world's own peoples
steps.words: A world's people is its own, even one named after a rulebook race: read its card, not the book. RP is race points, the Race Builder's price; a race above this table's limit is greyed out.

buttons.label: details
buttons.words: A race's whole card: its traits, languages and peoples.

buttons.label: ← back
buttons.words: Leaves the creator; what you chose here is not kept.

steps.title: Before this
steps.words: A background is optional and worth taking: a little skill, and above all somebody in this world who already knows you. The names fill in from the world when the game begins.

steps.title: Class
steps.words: Each card shows the class's hit die, attack bonus, skill ranks and whether it casts. Homebrew classes are here too. Crafts such as herbalism are not picked here: they grow by use beside any class.

steps.title: Paths and choices
steps.words: Some classes follow paths. The first you pick is Path A, from first level; the second is Path B, which opens at the level its slot names. Below come any other choices the class makes at first level.

steps.title: Point buy
steps.words: Raise or lower each score with its + and −. Spent counts the cost against this table's budget, which the Rulesets bench sets; it turns red when you are over. The race's adjustments land after, shown as becomes.

steps.title: Checked by the rules
steps.words: The counts here keep pace as you go. The rules check the whole character when you make them, and list everything wrong with its reason; nothing is made until it is put right.

source.literal: the submit round-trips the whole form and renders every problem at once

steps.title: Favoured class
steps.words: Your class is your favoured class: each level in it gives a hit point or a skill rank, your choice, and you choose again at every level.

steps.title: Ranks
steps.words: Tick a skill to put a rank in it. The count says how many you have: your class's ranks plus your Intelligence, and more for some peoples. Your class skills are in gold, and more ranks come with every level.

steps.title: The ?
steps.words: Hover over or press a skill's ? to see what it does in this game, not only in the book: what makes the engine roll it, and what it does not do yet.

buttons.label: Spells & feats →
buttons.words: On to feats and spells, worked out from everything above.

steps.title: Only what they can take
steps.words: This page asks the rules what this character qualifies for, so the list holds only feats they can take now. Tick the box to see the rest too, each with what it still needs.

controls.label: Show the ones they cannot take yet

source.literal: what the SERVER said this character qualifies for

steps.title: Finding one
steps.words: Narrow the list by typing here, or with the chips, which count each kind; previous and next turn its pages. Press a feat to take it, and its ✕ above to give it back. The count says how many feats you have.

steps.title: Spells and domains
steps.words: A caster with spells known picks them below, with a count for each spell level; what they prepare is chosen at the table each morning. A cleric, who prepares from the whole list, picks only domains here.

buttons.label: Create & outfit →
buttons.words: Makes them, then on to spending their starting purse.

buttons.label: Create for the roster
buttons.words: Makes them and puts them on the roster for later.

buttons.label: ← back to who they are
buttons.words: Back to the first page; nothing chosen is lost.

steps.title: Purse and basket
steps.words: Their starting purse is all the gear they get. Put things in the basket with + and −, and the bar shows what would be left. What is not spent stays in the purse for the road.

source.literal: What is not spent stays in the purse.

steps.title: The shelves
steps.words: Weapons, armour, shields and gear at the rulebook's prices. Something they are not trained in is still for sale and says so; it fights at a penalty. Sort can put what they are trained in first.

steps.title: Only before the first turn
steps.words: Carrying shows what they already have. This page is for a new character only: once their game begins it closes to them, and gear comes from the shops and stalls in town.

source.literal: the outfitter is closed to them

buttons.label: Buy the basket
buttons.words: Pays for everything in it. Buy or empty it before leaving.

buttons.label: Begin the sandbox →
buttons.words: Starts the game; the opening scene can take a minute to write.

buttons.label: Keep on the shelf
buttons.words: Back home; their game can start later.

steps.title: Start from
steps.words: Start from a template, or open a class that already exists. A simple class fills in the first sections and stops; the ones under Advanced are for classes that need them.

steps.title: The sections
steps.words: Down the side are the class's sections, field by field. A number beside one is how many problems it has. JSON, at the foot, is the file exactly as it will be written; paste one in and press Apply.

steps.title: Sound or not
steps.words: The box at the top checks the class as you work. Sound means it loads, a character can be made in it, and it levels all the way. Press a problem to go to its section; nothing is kept until they are gone.

source.literal: Nothing is kept until they are gone.

buttons.label: Keep this class
buttons.words: Saves it to your homebrew, once it is sound.

steps.title: Start from a race
steps.words: Pick a race that exists and load it: everything is copied but the name. The shipped file is never changed; editing one writes your own copy beside it.

steps.title: Everything is picked
steps.words: You type only the name. Type, size, speed, the Race Builder's ability options, a bonus feat or skill rank, and languages are all picked. The anatomy is the eidolon's evolutions, and free here.

steps.title: The summary
steps.words: The summary adds the race up as the sheet will read it. This table's race point limit, set on the Rulesets bench, is said beneath it.

buttons.label: Save to my homebrew
buttons.words: Saves it, or says what is missing first.

steps.title: Start from a spell
steps.words: Search by name, pick a spell and load it: every field is copied but the name, which is yours to give. Or leave the list on an empty spell and begin from nothing.

steps.title: Every field
steps.words: Every field a spell has, a star on the ones it must have. The engine casts it with real slots, caster level and save DC; what it does beyond that stays its own words, which the engine does not turn into numbers.

buttons.label: Save to my homebrew
buttons.words: Saves it, castable at once and marked as yours, or says what is missing.
